'''''The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou''''' is a 2004 American [[adventure film|adventure]] [[comedy-drama|comedy-drama film]] written by [[Wes Anderson]] and [[Noah Baumbach]] and directed by Anderson.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/12/10/movies/10life.html?_r=1|work=The New York Times|title=A Seagoing Showcase of Human Collectibles|author=A. O. Scott|date=December 10, 2004}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/topic/mmx-041224-movies-review-mw-aquatic,0,4263604.story?track=rss-topicgallery|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130128005258/http://www.latimes.com/topic/mmx-041224-movies-review-mw-aquatic,0,4263604.story?track=rss-topicgallery|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 28, 2013|title='The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou'|author=Michael Wilmington|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=December 22, 2004}}</ref> It is Anderson's fourth feature-length film and was released in the United States on December 25, 2004.

The film stars [[Bill Murray]] as Steve Zissou, an eccentric [[Oceanography|oceanographer]] who sets out with his crew to exact revenge on the "jaguar shark" that ate his partner Esteban. Zissou is both a [[parody]] of and [[Homage (arts)|homage]] to French diving pioneer [[Jacques Cousteau]], to whom the film is dedicated.

The film also features [[Owen Wilson]], [[Cate Blanchett]], [[Willem Dafoe]], [[Michael Gambon]], [[Jeff Goldblum]], [[Anjelica Huston]], and [[Bud Cort]]. [[Seu Jorge]] has a minor part, but contributes heavily to the [[The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou (soundtrack)|film's soundtrack]]. It was filmed in and around [[Rome]], [[Naples]], [[Ponza]], and the [[Italian Riviera]].<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0362270/locations/ |title=The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou (2004) - Filming & production - IMDb |language=en-US |access-date=2026-02-12 |via=www.imdb.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-12-24 |title=32 Facts About The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou |url=https://www.mentalfloss.com/article/60795/32-facts-about-life-aquatic-steve-zissou |access-date=2026-02-12 |website=Mental Floss |language=en-US}}</ref>

The film was released to mixed reviews and was a [[box office flop]].<ref name="autogenerated2005">{{cite news|last=Blake|first=Jason|date=October 4, 2005|title=The Life Aquatic With Steve Zissou - Film Reviews - Film - Entertainment|language=en|newspaper=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]|url=https://www.smh.com.au/news/film-reviews/the-life-aquatic-with-steve-zissou/2005/10/04/1128391225506.html|access-date=June 11, 2018}}</ref> In the decade following its release it has garnered a [[cult following]], and is now viewed more positively by both critics and fans.<ref name="avfilmclub">{{Cite web |date=2014-05-28 |title=Wes Anderson's The Life Aquatic is much better than its initial reviews claimed |url=https://www.avclub.com/wes-anderson-s-the-life-aquatic-is-much-better-than-its-1798180581 |access-date=2024-07-13 |website=The A.V. Club |language=en}}</ref><ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite web|last=VanDerWerff|first=Emily|date=Mar 26, 2017|title=The Life Aquatic might not be Wes Anderson's best film. But it is his greatest.|url=https://www.vox.com/culture/2017/3/26/15043152/the-life-aquatic-wes-anderson-best|access-date=June 11, 2018|website=[[Vox (website)|Vox]]}}</ref><ref name="esquire1">{{cite magazine|last=Reed|first=Ryan|date=December 24, 2014|title=In Defense of The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou, 10 Years Later|url=https://www.esquire.com/entertainment/movies/reviews/a31608/the-life-aquatic-10-years-later/|magazine=[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]|language=en-US|access-date=June 11, 2018}}</ref><ref name="jones1">{{cite web |url=https://footwearnews.com/2017/focus/athletic-outdoor/adidas-finally-releases-life-aquatic-with-steve-zissou-shoes-382735/|title=Adidas Finally Releases the Shoes From Cult Classic 'The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou' |last=Jones |first=Riley |date=June 26, 2017 |website=Footwear News |language=en-US |access-date=June 11, 2018}}</ref>

==Plot==
While [[Oceanography|oceanographer]] Steve Zissou is working on his latest documentary at sea, his best friend and chief diver, Esteban du Plantier, is devoured by a 10-meter-long, spotted creature Zissou describes as a "jaguar shark". For his next project, Zissou is determined to document the shark's destruction.

The crew aboard Zissou's aging [[research vessel]] ''Belafonte'' includes his estranged wife Eleanor, chief strategist and financial backer; Pelé dos Santos, a safety expert and Brazilian guitarist who sings [[David Bowie]] songs in Portuguese; and Klaus Daimler, the German first mate who views Zissou and Esteban as father figures. Other crew members include Vikram Ray, cameraman; Bobby Ogata, frogman; Vladimir Wolodarsky, physicist and soundtrack composer; Renzo Pietro, sound man; and Anne-Marie Sakowitz, a script girl. Also included is a recent group of unpaid interns from the University of North [[Alaska]]. However, the "Team Zissou" venture has hit a decline, having not released a successful documentary in nine years.

Ned Plimpton, a longtime Zissou fan whose mother has recently died, believes that Zissou is his father. After they meet at Zissou's latest premiere, Ned takes annual leave from his job as an airline pilot in [[Kentucky]] to join his crew. As Oseary Drakoulias, Zissou's producer, cannot find a financier for their latest documentary, Ned offers his inheritance. Eleanor feels her husband is manipulating Ned and leaves.

Pregnant reporter Jane Winslett-Richardson comes to chronicle the voyage. Both Ned and Zissou are attracted to Jane and a [[love triangle]] develops between them. Klaus becomes jealous of the attention Zissou pays to Ned.

On their mission to find the jaguar shark, the ''Belafonte'' steals tracking equipment from a remote station owned by more successful oceanographer (also Eleanor's ex-husband and Zissou's nemesis) Alistair Hennessey. They then sail into unprotected waters and are attacked by Filipino pirates, who steal Ned's money and kidnap Bill Ubell, "a [[Completion guarantee|bond company]] stooge" assigned to the project. They are then rescued by Hennessey and towed to Port-au-Patois.<ref group=Note name=Note01/> Sakowitz, along with all but one of the interns, jumps ship once they reach port.

Zissou persuades Eleanor to rejoin the ''Belafonte'' and then leads the crew on a rescue mission. They track Bill to an abandoned hotel on a remote island, saving him along with Hennessey, whom the pirates have also kidnapped. Ned and Zissou make one last search for the shark in the ship's helicopter, but the aircraft malfunctions and they crash. Ned dies from his injuries and is [[Burial at sea|buried at sea]]. Prior to Ned's death, Eleanor revealed to Jane that Zissou is [[Infertility|sterile]] and therefore Ned could not have been his son.

Zissou finally tracks down the shark in a [[submersible]] but decides not to kill it, both because of its beauty and being out of dynamite. He ponders, "I wonder if it remembers me," and is overcome with emotion. Eleanor silently comforts him, as does Jane and the rest of the crew. At the premiere of the finished documentary (which is dedicated to Ned, who is acknowledged as Zissou's son), Zissou receives a standing ovation while waiting outside the theater for the premiere to finish. The crew returns triumphantly to the ship.

==Production==
[[File:ZISSOU COSTUME.jpg|thumb|Costume worn by Steve Zissou ([[Bill Murray]]) at the [[Academy Museum of Motion Pictures|Academy Museum]] in [[Los Angeles|Los Angeles, California]].]]
===Literary inspiration===
Though the characters were inspired by such American novels as ''[[The Great Gatsby]]'' and ''[[The Magnificent Ambersons]],'' the plot has been compared to ''[[Moby-Dick]].''<ref>{{cite journal | last=Govender | first=Dyalan | title=Wes Anderson's ''The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou'' and Melville's ''Moby Dick'': A Comparative Study | journal=[[Literature/Film Quarterly]] | volume=36 | issue=1 | pages=61–67}}</ref>

Writing about the metaphorical aspects of the film's setting—somewhere in the Mediterranean—film critic Elena Past says that the underwater scenes, because they are central to the storyline, make ''The Life Aquatic'' similar in some ways to ''[[Respiro]].'' Both films set out a "Mediterranean state of being" where "having left the security of land, the characters in both films are suddenly confronted with the precarious nature of human existence, as the films that depict them tackle the challenges of representing the submarine world."<ref>{{cite journal | last=Past | first=Elena | title=Lives Aquatic: Mediterranean Cinema and an Ethics of Underwater Existence | journal=[[Cinema Journal]] | volume=48 | issue=3 | date=Spring 2009 | pages=52–65 | doi=10.1353/cj.0.0104| s2cid=144151939 }}</ref>

===Casting===
[[James Gray (director)|James Gray]] originally signed on to play Wolodarsky but he left when he learned that he was going to spend five months in Italy.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.indiewire.com/2013/10/nyff-james-gray-almost-appeared-in-wes-andersons-the-life-aquatic-talks-the-immigrant-with-joaquin-phoenix-92903/ | title=NYFF: James Gray Almost Appeared in Wes Anderson's 'The Life Aquatic,' Talks 'The Immigrant' with Joaquin Phoenix | date=October 7, 2013 }}</ref>

===Exotic lifeforms===
In addition to the luminescent-spotted jaguar shark, other fictional lifeforms (some [[stop motion|stop-motion-animated]]) are cited and appear throughout the film, such as the rhinestone bluefin, crayon ponyfish, wild snow-mongoose, electric jellyfish, and sugar crabs. The animation work was done by [[Henry Selick]].{{Citation needed|date=February 2026}}

===Music{{anchor|Music|Score}}===
{{Main|The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou (soundtrack)|The Life Aquatic Studio Sessions}}
The soundtrack to ''The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou'' contains a style typical of other Wes Anderson films. [[Mark Mothersbaugh]], a member of [[Devo]], composed the score, as he has for many of Anderson's other films. The film also features many rock songs from the 1960s-1980s, and several instrumental pieces composed by [[Sven Libaek]] for the underwater documentary television series ''Inner Space.'' Additionally, the film and soundtrack feature [[Seu Jorge]] performing [[David Bowie]] songs in Portuguese on the acoustic guitar. Jorge, who also plays the character of Pelé dos Santos, performs some of these cover songs live, in character during the film, mostly with modified lyrics reflecting Jorge's own experiences working on the film.<ref>{{cite web | date = May 4, 2005 | last = Carle | first = Chris | title = Review: The Life Aquatic With Steve Zissou Original Soundtrack | url = http://music.ign.com/articles/604/604056p1.html | work = [[IGN]] | publisher = [[News Corporation (1980–2013)|News Corporation]] | access-date = May 23, 2008 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071223144543/http://music.ign.com/articles/604/604056p1.html | archive-date = December 23, 2007}}</ref> The ending scene depicting the beauty of the shark features the song "[[Ágætis byrjun|Starálfur]]" by [[Sigur Rós]].

''The Life Aquatic'' is Anderson's first film not to feature a [[Rolling Stones]] song.

==Reception==

===Box office===
The film grossed a total of $24,020,403 domestically after twelve weeks in release, less than half its $50 million production budget. It took in a further $10,788,000 internationally, bringing the total gross to $34,808,403.<ref name="mojo">{{cite web | title = The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou| url = https://boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=lifeaquatic.htm | website = [[Box Office Mojo]] | publisher = [[Amazon.com]]|access-date=September 3, 2015}}</ref>

===Critical response {{anchor|Critics}}===
Initial reviews of the film were mixed. The film has a 57% approval rating on [[Rotten Tomatoes]], based on 226 reviews, with an average rating of 6.10/10; the website's consensus states: "Much like the titular oceanographer, ''The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou''{{'}}s overt irony may come off as smug and artificial – but for fans of Wes Anderson's unique brand of whimsy, it might be worth the dive."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/life_aquatic/ |title=Life Aquatic at Rotten Tomatoes |website=Rotten Tomatoes|access-date=April 22, 2021}}</ref> The film has a 62/100 [[weighted average]] score on [[Metacritic]], indicating "generally favorable reviews".<ref>{{Metacritic film}}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "D" on an A+ to F scale.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Home |url=https://www.cinemascore.com/ |access-date=2022-03-20 |website=[[CinemaScore]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

[[Anthony Lane]], a film reviewer for ''[[The New Yorker]],'' agreed with the conventional criticism of Anderson's [[deadpan]] style: that the underreaction of Anderson's characters used to be "hip" but has now become "frozen into a mannerism." He said that "some stretches of action" in the film are being "lightly held within quotation marks," with an "unmistakable air of playacting" in even the most violent scenes. He also criticized the film's deliberately "weird" set ups, which leave the viewer with "the impression of having nearly drowned in some secret and melancholy game."<ref>{{cite magazine| last = Lane | first = Anthony | author-link = Anthony Lane | title = Go Fish: "The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou" | magazine = [[The New Yorker]] | volume = 80 | issue = 43 | date = January 17, 2005 | pages = 96–97 | url = https://www.newyorker.com/archive/2005/01/17/050117crci_cinema | access-date = September 14, 2009}}</ref>

In the years since its initial release it has developed a [[cult following]],<ref name="jones1"/><ref name="autogenerated2005"/> and it underwent a critical reevaluation. Many critics view it more favorably, and some, such as Mike D'Angelo of ''[[The A.V. Club]],'' consider the film to still be "undervalued" when compared to the rest of Anderson's filmography.<ref name="avfilmclub"/><ref name="autogenerated1"/><ref name="esquire1"/>

In 2025, it was one of the films voted for the "Readers' Choice" edition of ''[[The New York Times]]''{{'}} list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century," finishing at number 226.<ref>{{cite web |title=Readers Choose Their Top Movies of the 21st Century |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/movies/readers-movies-21st-century.html |website=The New York Times |access-date=2 July 2025}}</ref>

==Home media==
The DVD of the film was released by the [[Criterion Collection]] on May 10, 2005 as its 300th title, in both 1-disc version and a 2-disc versions. This is Anderson's third film to be released in the collection, after ''[[Rushmore (film)|Rushmore]]'' and ''[[The Royal Tenenbaums]].''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.criterion.com/explore/169-wes-anderson |title=Wes Anderson - Explore - The Criterion Collection |publisher=Criterion.com |access-date=June 2, 2014}}</ref> The Criterion [[Blu-ray]] was released on May 27, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blu-ray.com/movies/The-Life-Aquatic-with-Steve-Zissou-Blu-ray/74285/|title=The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou Blu-ray |publisher=Blu-ray.com |access-date=June 2, 2014}}</ref> It was released on [[Ultra HD Blu-ray]] by Criterion on September 30, 2025, as part of the ten film collection ''The Wes Anderson Archive: Ten Films, Twenty-Five Years''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zavaleta |first=Jonathan |date=2025-06-02 |title=The $500 Wes Anderson Criterion Box Set Is Cinephile Catnip |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/product-recommendations/lifestyle/wes-anderson-criterion-box-set-where-to-buy-1235352817/ |access-date=2025-06-03 |website=Rolling Stone |language=en-US}}</ref>

==In popular culture==
{{in popular culture|date=December 2025}}
* The name of Mexican rock band [[Belafonte Sensacional]] is inspired, in part, by the film.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.tierraadentro.cultura.gob.mx/belafonte-sensacional-folk-mexicano-on-the-road/|title=Belafonte sensacional: folk mexicano On the road (Belafonte Sensacional: Mexican folk on the road)|last=Hidalgo|first=Juan Carlos|date=2014-05-15|website=Tierra Adentro magazine|language=es-ES|access-date=2018-12-24}}</ref>
* ''[[Epic Rap Battles of History]]'' released a [[rap battle]] between Jacques Cousteau and [[Steve Irwin]]. In one of Cousteau's flex bars, he references ''The Life Aquatic'' saying, "I'm so cool, Bill Murray played me in the movie."
* The title of an episode of the animated sitcom ''[[Family Guy]]'', "[[The Tan Aquatic with Steve Zissou]]", is a reference to the film.
* The song "Alan Forever" on [[Lupe Fiasco]]'s album ''[[DROGAS WAVE]]'' imagines an alternate reality for [[Alan Kurdi]], in which he survived his emigration from [[Syria]] and "might be the next Steve Zissou or maybe Jacques Cousteau."
* The ocean-themed 13th major update released for the video game ''[[Minecraft]]'' was titled "Update Aquatic" in reference to the film.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Östergård |first1=Adrian |title=Update Aquatic is out on Java! |url=https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/update-aquatic-out-java |website=Minecraft |date=2018-07-22}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Hillier |first1=Brenna |title=Minecraft: The Update Aquatic adds dolphins, shipwrecks, new water physics, trident weapon and more |url=https://www.vg247.com/minecraft-the-update-aquatic-adds-dolphins-shipwrecks-new-water-physics-trident-weapon-and-more |website=VG247 |language=en |date=November 20, 2017}}</ref>
* The song "Zissou" by [[Hayley Williams]] (solo artist and frontwoman of the band [[Paramore]])  is named in reference to the movie and also mentions "Team Zissou" in the first verse.
* Rapper [[Logic (rapper)|Logic]] used the poster as inspiration for the cover art to his sophomore album, ''[[The Incredible True Story]]''.
